property_summary: After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the configured state variable remains true.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved(sender, target, emergency), the configured state variable is true if the reference contract is used, but false in the mutant.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the return value of configured() mirrors whether the caller was a successful proposal.
After assertGovernanceApproved reverts, the configured state variable remains unchanged from before the call.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the configured getter returns true.
After a successful call to assertGovernanceApproved, the configured getter returns true.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the DAO state variable remains unchanged from its value set by the constructor (or subsequent setDAO calls).
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the getter for the address returned by c.DAO() should be the address set by a prior setDAO call, regardless of the fuzz parameters.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with any parameters, the stored DAO address must be the same as it was before the call (setDAO should not change DAO).
After setDAO, the DAO address must remain unchanged by any subsequent call to assertGovernanceApproved, regardless of fuzz parameters.
After any sequence of calls ending with assertGovernanceApproved, the address of the pendingFlashGovernance asset for the target-sender pair must equal the configured flashGovernanceConfig.asset.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with any arguments, the flashGovernanceConfig.asset stored in pendingFlashDecision[target][sender] must equal the current flashGovernanceConfig.asset.
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved, the value of c.setDAO() should match the originally deployed DAO.
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved, the configured state variable must remain true.
After calling setDAO(), the value of c.DAO() should equal the last address provided to setDAO().
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the configured state variable must remain true if it was true before the call.
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved, the configured state variable must remain true.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with emergency=false, the state variable DAO remains the same as before the call.
After any call to setDAO, the configured state variable must be false when the caller is not the DAO and the contract is not configured.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the configured state variable must be false when DAO equals address(this) and the call was made by DAO.
After assertGovernanceApproved is called, the configured state variable must be false if DAO is the caller and configured was false before the call.
After any call to setDAO, the configured state variable must remain unchanged (i.e., the setDAO function must never modify configured).
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the internal state variable 'governer' should reflect the last used DAO's flash governor, but the buggy code sets it to address(0) regardless.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the value of c.DAO() should remain the same as the address used to deploy the contract.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the public getter for the governer field should match the flash governor retrieved from the DAO (which is this test contract, returning itself).
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the public getter c.DAO() equals the address used to deploy the contract (address(this)).
After any call to setDAO, the flashGovernanceConfig.amount should remain unchanged, but the bug zeros the governer without updating config, which does not affect amount.
If address X is set as governed via assertGovernanceApproved for target Y, then governed[X] should be set only when X appears in the governables array.

When assertGovernanceApproved reverts, the governed mapping for the caller remains unchanged (any key other than the caller is unaffected). The bug changes governed[msg.sender] inside the setGoverned loop, which persists even if assertGovernanceApproved later reverts, breaking this rule.
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved that reverts, the governed mapping for any address that was passed in the governables array of the most recent setGoverned call remains unchanged.

After any sequence of calls ending with assertGovernanceApproved, for each address X that appears in the governables array of the last setGoverned call, governed[X] equals the corresponding isGoverned value.
For any address K, if K was never passed as the first element of governables in any setGoverned call, then governed[K] remains false after any sequence of calls ending with assertGovernanceApproved.
Calling assertGovernanceApproved with a sender that is not the DAO and not governed, and with flashGovernanceConfig.amount == 0, the call reverts in P but does not revert in M.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with a governed sender, the governed mapping for that sender remains unchanged.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with a governed sender, the governed mapping for that sender is still true.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the governed mapping for the sender must remain true if it was true before the call (i.e., the function cannot make a governed address become ungoverned).
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with a sender that is the DAO, the call should succeed regardless of the flash governance config amount being zero.
The governed mapping at the caller address is set to true after calling assertGovernanceApproved with the same address as target.
The governed mapping for the msg.sender is set correctly after setGoverned call.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved by a non-DAO sender whose target is the sender itself, the sender is marked as governed (governed[sender] == true).
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved by a user that is the DAO (the test contract), the governed mapping for the first address is never set to true when the original address array has length 1.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the state mapping governed for an arbitrary address does not revert the contract.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, all addresses in the governables array have their governed mapping set correctly without out-of-bounds access
After a successful call to assertGovernanceApproved, the number of addresses that are governed can be no more than the length of the last governables array used in setGoverned.

After any number of setGoverned calls followed by a call to assertGovernanceApproved, the governed mapping for any address that was never in any governables array used in a setGoverned call must remain false.

After calling assertGovernanceApproved with emergency=true, the function should not revert and the pending flash decision should have unlockTime equal to flashGovernanceConfig.unlockTime + block.timestamp.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the governed mapping for any address is always true if it was true before, regardless of the fuzz parameters.
After assertGovernanceApproved, the mapping returns true for addresses that were previously set to true in setGoverned, regardless of the caller.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the governed mapping remains unchanged for any address that was not previously set.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the governed mapping for any address that was previously set to true via setGoverned remains true, regardless of the fuzz parameters.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the governed mapping for any address remains unchanged from its initial state.
